q: Oh, poh! they might have been counted some how or other, unless indeed they were so numerous as to require all our people to stand sentinel round them.
1811 May 29, William Cobbett, “Summary of Politics”, in Cobbett's Weekly Political Register, volume 19, number 43, page 1323:
Poh, it's from your sister at Lyons, and contains good news: read it.
1856, Oliver Goldsmith, The Works of Oliver Goldsmith, page 69:
"Oh poh!" said Benny. "When I grow up, I'm goin' to have a span!"
1877, Abby Morton Diaz, Brother Billy, Dorry Baker, and Bubby Short, page 208:
"Poh, poh! it's a mere trifle, I repeat," Tibbits rejoined.
1857, William Harrison Ainsworth, The Spendthrift: A Tale, page 298:
She brought fresh green chillies with her every day and cooked me poha for breakfast.
2020, Avni Doshi, Burnt Sugar, Hamish Hamilton, page 111:
I found in an old-fashioned garden overlooking the beach and the pohutukawa trees, the mulberry tree with leaves to feed our ‘charges’, and a kindly owner willing to give me supplies of leaves.
1984, Janet Frame, An Angel at my Table, Virago, published 2024, page 279:
On the map, this road ends with the representation of a sacred pōhutukawa tree.
